newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Dec durable goods orders fell 1.7 pct.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Dec durable goods orders fell 1.7 pct.

text.p: U.S. Commerce Department seasonally adjusted data on durable goods orders, with percent changes from prior months.
PERCENT CHANGES: Dec Nov--Rev from Oct

NEW ORDERS-PCT CHANGES Dec Nov--Rev from Oct
Wall Street economists had expected December durable goods orders to rise 1.2 percent. Excluding defense orders, they expected a 2.2 percent increase.
For all of 1996, U.S. durable goods orders rose 5.5 percent after a 7.2 percent rise in 1995, the department said. It was the smallest yearly increase since a 5.4 percent rise in 1993.

The declines in durables orders in December and November were the first back-to-back declines since a drop of 0.1 percent in January 1996 and a 2.5 percent decline in February. The drop in durable goods orders in December was the seventh decrease for 1996.
Also, in the transportation component, the department said increases in shipbuilding and tanks and railroad equipment more than offset decreases in motor vehicles and parts, and aircraft and parts.

For December durable goods, orders for electronic and electrical equipment showed the largest decrease, falling by $3.5 billion, or 12.5 percent, to $24.5 billion. The department said that was due mostly to a drop in orders for communication equipment and electronic components.
